sections.content:
35,305 people

were counted on the census as "IT project managers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
IT project managers manage, coordinate and technically supervise specific IT projects of a set duration and/or budget.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 40 to 44 years. Of the whole working population 10.9% were aged 40 to 44 years. For people working as "IT project managers", 15.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "IT project managers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "IT project managers" included:

  • business and financial project management professionals
  • managers in logistics
  • human resource managers and directors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "IT project managers" there were more men than women (65.7% compared with 34.3%).

This means "IT project managers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 65.7% and women made up 34.3% of "IT project managers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "IT project managers" included:

  • police officers (sergeant and below)
  • footwear and leather working trades
  • managers and directors in the creative industries

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "IT project managers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "IT project managers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "IT project managers", 6.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (93.8% compared with 6.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92%) than self-employed (8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
